newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's Bulbank to buy stake in ailing bank.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's Bulbank to buy stake in ailing bank.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest commercial bank Bulbank (Bulgarian Foreign Trade Bank) is in discussions to acquire a 66 percent stake in the troubled Economic Bank Stopanska Banka A.D., a government official said on Tuesday.

"We have offered Bulbank to buy the 66 percent held by the Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) in the Economic Bank," newly appointed BCC board chairman and deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev told reporters.
Bulbank officials confirmed that they were negotiating such an acquisition, but declined to elaborate. It is not yet clear how Economic Bank's foreign debts would be restructured.
The BCC, set up to merge and privatise some of the country's numerous troubled banks, manages state equity in nine local commercial banks.

The central bank has placed the Economic Bank under special supervision with eight other banks to establish their financial state and decide whether to seek their insolvency through courts or sell them.

The Economic Bank posted a cumulative loss of 11.3 billion levs up to the end of August this year, a bank report showed. Its capital to risk assets ratio stood at minus 56.6 percent, well below the Basle banking standards of plus eight percent.

The bank's debts to foreign creditors concentrated in Italian and Austrian banks amount to about $170 million and this year's payments on them stand at around $9 million. It is unclear whether Economic Bank has covered these annual payments.

Bulbank, which has so far weathered the national banking crisis, posted 788 million levs pre-tax profit for 1995. Its capital totalled 44.2 billion levs at the end of last year with shareholders' equity amounting to 5.0 billion levs.
